conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're asking about?** (Or if you have multiple children, tell me about their ages)

Please let me know:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my three kids.

I've got Alex who's 5, Blake who's 17, and Charlie who's 19.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll help you check eligibility for all three of your children. Let me work through the eligibility requirements for each of them.

Since your children are different ages, they fall into different categories:
- **Alex (age 5)**: Under 16
- **Blake (age 17)**: 16-19 years old
- **Charlie (age 19)**: 16-19 years old

Let me start by checking the requirements for each age group. I'll begin with some questions about your situation.

**First, let me ask about Alex (age 5):**

Since Alex is under 16, they automatically qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes. However, I need to check a few things about your circumstances.

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for looking after Alex?** (i.e., are you the main carer/parent living with the child)

Also, to help me with Blake and Charlie, I need to know:

**For Blake (age 17): Is Blake currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

**For Charlie (age 19): Is Charlie currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

Please answer these questions so I can check the specific eligibility requirements for each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I'm the main parent - all three of them live at home with me.

As for Blake, no, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't doing anything formal right now.

Charlie though, yes - she's in full-time education. She's doing her A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me navigate through the eligibility requirements for each child based on what you've told me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I have the specific rules. Let me ask about Alex first:

**For Alex (age 5):** Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work? (This is typically "yes" for a 5-year-old, but I need to confirm)

Also, I need to check a couple more things:

**For Blake (age 17):** Since Blake is not in education or training, I need to ask - **is Blake working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

**For Charlie (age 19):** Great to know Charlie is in full-time A-levels. I need to confirm: **Is Charlie studying at least 12 hours per week in supervised study?** (A-levels are typically 15+ hours, so this should be yes, but I need to confirm)

Also, I need to gather some information about your household:

**What is your household's annual income? Specifically, do you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year?** (This affects payment, not eligibility, but is important to know)

Please provide these details so I can complete the assessment for all three children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
For Alex, no, she's definitely not working - she's only 5! She's in primary school.

Blake isn't working full-time either. He just does a Saturday shift at the local shop, nothing more than that.

And yes, Charlie's doing full A-levels at sixth form - it's definitely more than 12 hours a week of proper supervised study.

As for income, no, neither my partner nor I earn over £60,000 a year.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for those details. Let me navigate through the eligibility requirements for each child now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check another requirement:

**For Alex and Blake: Are neither of them receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own right?** (i.e., they don't have their own benefits claim)

Once you confirm this, I can continue with the next checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of them receive any benefits in their own right. They're just my dependents.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**For Alex, Blake, and Charlie: Are none of them in an apprenticeship?** (Since Blake is just doing a Saturday shop job and Charlie is in A-levels, I expect the answer is no for all, but I need to confirm)

Also, to complete this check - **which part of the UK do you live in: England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?** (This matters for the apprenticeship rules)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
That's right - none of them are doing apprenticeships. Blake's just doing his Saturday shift at the shop, and Charlie's focused on her A-levels.

We live in England - in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for confirming. Now let me move to the next stage of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check the residency requirements for you as the claimant:

**Do you normally live in the UK?** (I know you live in Manchester, but I'm asking to confirm you normally reside in the UK - for example, you're not living abroad most of the time)

This is a key requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I normally live in the UK. Manchester is my home, we're here all the time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for each child:

**You mentioned all three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) live at home with you - is that correct?** This means you are living with them and responsible for their upkeep, which satisfies this requirement.

Let me confirm this is the case for all three before we move to the next check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - all three of them live at home with me. I'm their parent and I look after them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other claimants:

**Is anyone else (such as your partner, another parent, or guardian) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, Blake, or Charlie?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for any of them. It's just me looking after them and I'm the one wanting to claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent

Great! Now I need to check the living situation for each child:

**Are Alex, Blake, and Charlie all living at home with you normally?** Or are any of them:
- Currently in hospital?
- In foster care or other care arrangements?
- Living away from home in any special circumstances?

I'm assuming they're all living at home with you normally, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - they're all living at home with me normally. None of them are in hospital, foster care, or anything like that. Just a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent

Excellent! We're nearly at the end of the assessment. One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex, Blake, or Charlie's accommodation or maintenance?** (In other words, you're not receiving any council support for housing or care for any of them - you're funding their upkeep yourself or with your partner)

I'm assuming the answer is yes since this is a normal family situation, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance. I'm supporting them myself as their parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me work through the specific requirements for Blake and Charlie, since they're in the 16-19 age group and have different circumstances.

conversation.text: Excellent! That outcome applies to Alex. However, I need to check the specific requirements for Blake and Charlie since they're in a different age group. Let me go back and navigate through the 16-19 age checks for them.

conversation.text:
Let me get back to the routing node to check Blake and Charlie's eligibility. I need to restart the navigation for them since they're in the 16-19 age bracket.

Based on the information you've provided, let me work through the specific eligibility for each child:

**For Alex (age 5):**
✅ **ELIGIBLE** - Alex meets all Child Benefit requirements as a child under 16

**For Blake (age 17):**
- Blake is 16-19 years old and NOT in approved education or training
- Blake is working less than 24 hours per week (Saturday shop job only)
- This means Blake does NOT qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes since he's left school and isn't in approved education or training

**For Charlie (age 19):**
- Charlie is 16-19 years old and IS in full-time A-levels (approved education)
- Charlie is studying more than 12 hours per week of supervised study
- Charlie meets the education requirements for Child Benefit eligibility
- ✅ **ELIGIBLE** - Charlie qualifies because she's in approved full-time education

Let me now provide you with the final assessment:

conversation.text:
## Final Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment

Thank you for providing all the information needed. Here's your eligibility outcome:

### **Summary:**
✅ **ELIGIBLE for 2 out of 3 children: Alex and Charlie**

---

### **Individual Results:**

#### **Alex (Age 5) - ✅ ELIGIBLE**
- Alex automatically qualifies as a child under 16
- All requirements are met: not working full-time, not receiving benefits, living at home with you, and you meet all claimant requirements
- **You can claim Child Benefit for Alex**

#### **Blake (Age 17) - ❌ NOT ELIGIBLE**
- Although Blake is under 20, he is not in approved full-time education or training
- Blake left school and is only working a part-time Saturday job
- **The rule:** For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit is only payable if they are in approved full-time education or training
- **You cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake** until he returns to approved education/training or reaches eligibility through another route

#### **Charlie (Age 19) - ✅ ELIGIBLE**
- Charlie is in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- A-levels are an approved education level
- Charlie meets the minimum 12+ hours per week supervised study requirement
- **You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie**

---

### **What You Need to Do Next:**

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** at [gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
   - You can apply online or by post using form CH2
   - Apply for both **Alex** and **Charlie**

2. **Documentation needed:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Birth certificates or adoption certificates for Alex and Charlie
   - Evidence of Charlie's full-time education status (sixth form letter)

3. **Important:** Since neither you nor your partner earns over £60,000 annually, the High Income Child Benefit Charge does not apply to you.

---

### **About Blake:**
If Blake joins an approved education or training course in the future, you should inform HMRC as he would then become eligible. Keep receipts and documentation of his current employment for your records.

Do you have any questions about this assessment?

Alex is ELIGIBLE.

Blake is 17 years old and in the 16-19 age group. However, Blake is not in approved full-time education or training - he left school and is only working a Saturday shop job (less than 24 hours per week). For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit is only payable if they are in approved full-time education or training. Since Blake does not meet this requirement, Blake is NOT ELIGIBLE.

Charlie is 19 years old and in the 16-19 age group, currently in full-time A-levels at sixth form college. A-levels are approved education under the Child Benefit rules. Charlie is studying more than 12 hours per week in supervised study, which meets the minimum requirement. Charlie is not working full-time (assuming normal student status), is not receiving benefits in their own right, is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship, lives at home with the parent, and the parent meets all residency and responsibility requirements. Charlie is ELIGIBLE.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for two of your three children: Alex (age 5) and Charlie (age 19, in A-level education). Alex qualifies as a child under 16, which is an automatic qualifying category. Charlie qualifies because she is in approved full-time education (A-levels) and therefore extends her eligibility into the 16-19 age bracket. However, Blake (age 17) is not eligible because he is not in approved full-time education or training - he has left school and is only working part-time (Saturday shop job). For children aged 16-19 to qualify for Child Benefit, they must be in approved full-time education or training. You meet all other eligibility requirements: you normally live in the UK (Manchester), you are responsible for all three children and live with them, no other person is claiming for them, they are living normally at home, and the local council is not funding their upkeep."
